<TD WIDTH="4%"> <P STYLE="margin-bottom:1px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>5. </B></FONT></P></TD>
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="Top" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Q:</B></FONT></TD>
<TD> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>WHAT ARE THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED BY THE MASTER TRANSACTION AGREEMENT? </B></FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P
STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A:</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under the Master Transaction Agreement, AMD, Mubadala and ATIC intend to enter two distinct but related concurrent transactions. Mubadala (through its subsidiary WCH) will pay to
AMD an aggregate purchase price equal to (a) 58,000,000 multiplied by (b) the lesser of (A) the average of the closing prices per share of our common stock on the NYSE for the 20 trading days immediately prior to and including December 12, 2008 and
(B) the average of the closing prices per share of our common stock on the NYSE for the 20 trading days immediately prior to the closing date of the Transactions to acquire the Shares and the Warrants. At the same time, AMD and ATIC will enter into
a joint venture to form The Foundry Company, a global, independent semiconductor foundry to be headquartered in the United States. AMD will contribute assets, including its manufacturing facilities, its manufacturing employees, and intellectual
property rights to The Foundry Company. The Foundry Company will assume approximately $1.2 billion in debt from AMD. ATIC will invest $2.1 billion to purchase its stake in The Foundry Company, of which it will invest $1.4 billion directly in the new
entity and the remainder will be paid to AMD to purchase additional shares in The Foundry Company. ATIC&#146;s investment in The Foundry Company will be separate from Mubadala&#146;s investment in AMD, and ATIC will not acquire any shares of AMD.
</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="Top" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Q:</B></FONT></TD>
<TD> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>WHO WILL OWN THE FOUNDRY COMPANY JOINT VENTURE? </B></FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P

<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A:</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">When the Transactions contemplated by the Master Transaction Agreement<I></I><B><I></I></B><I></I> close (the &#147;<I></I><B><I>Closing</I></B><I></I>&#148;), AMD and ATIC will
each own one half of the voting shares, and each will be entitled to elect four out of eight members of the board of directors of The Foundry Company. At the Closing, The Foundry Company will be owned 34.2% by AMD and 65.8% by ATIC on a fully
converted to common basis. ATIC&#146;s ownership will increase over time based on the differences in securities held by AMD and ATIC, and depending on whether AMD elects to invest proportionately with ATIC in future capital infusions.
</FONT></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="4%"> <P STYLE="margin-bottom:1px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>7. </B></FONT></P></TD>
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="Top" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Q:</B></FONT></TD>
<TD> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:1px" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>WHO ARE MUBADALA AND ATIC? </B></FONT></P></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR>
<TD WIDTH="4%"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></TD>
<TD WIDTH="4%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A:</FONT></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Mubadala is an investment and development company wholly owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi. Mubadala&#146;s mandate is to generate sustainable economic benefits for Abu Dhabi
through prudent commercially viable and profitable business ventures. Mubadala was established as an Abu Dhabi public joint stock company. </FONT></TD></TR></TABLE> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:8%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ATIC is a limited liability company established under the laws of Abu Dhabi and wholly owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi. ATIC is focused on making significant investments in the advanced technology sector, both
locally and internationally. Its mandate is to generate returns that deliver long-term benefits to the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. We have been informed by ATIC that it is anticipated that, prior to the Closing, ATIC will become an Abu Dhabi public joint
stock company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

Warrant Shares to WCH. The proposal to approve the issuance of the Shares, Warrants and Warrant Shares to WCH requires the affirmative vote of a majority of the votes cast, provided that the total vote cast on the proposal represents over 50% of the
outstanding common stock entitled to vote on the proposal. If you &#147;<B>ABSTAIN</B>&#148; from voting on the proposal, your shares will be counted for purposes of determining whether a quorum is present, but will not be counted as votes
&#147;<B>FOR</B>&#148; or &#147;<B>AGAINST</B>&#148; the proposal. Broker non-votes will be counted for purposes of determining whether a quorum is present, but will not be counted as votes <B>&#147;FOR&#148; </B>or <B>&#147;AGAINST&#148; </B>the
proposal. A broker non-vote occurs where the broker has not received instructions from the beneficial owner as to how such beneficial owner&#146;s shares are to be voted on the proposal and does not have discretionary authority to vote on the
proposal. Under the NYSE rules, brokers do not have discretionary authority to vote on the proposal to approve the issuance of the Shares, Warrants and Warrant Shares to WCH. If you complete the voting instructions and submit your proxy, the persons
named as proxies will follow your instructions. If you submit a proxy but do not specify your voting instructions, the persons named as proxies will vote your shares &#147;<B>FOR</B>&#148; the adoption of the proposal set forth in this proxy

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_2"></A>PROPOSAL 1&#151;ISSUANCE OF SHARES, WARRANTS AND WARRANT SHARES
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Unless the context otherwise requires, references in this proxy statement to &#147;AMD,&#148; &#147;we,&#148; &#147;our&#148; or
&#147;us&#148; refer to Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">We are asking our stockholders to consider and
approve the issuance of the Shares and Warrants to WCH pursuant to the Master Transaction Agreement and the issuance of the Warrant Shares upon exercise of the Warrants. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_3"></A>Purpose of Stockholder Approval of Our Issuance of the Shares, the Warrants and the Warrant Shares to WCH </B></FONT></P>  <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The approval of AMD&#146;s stockholders of the issuance of the Shares and the Warrants to WCH pursuant to the Master Transaction Agreement and the Warrant
Shares upon the exercise of the Warrants is a condition to the Closing. The Master Transaction Agreement requires AMD to obtain stockholder approval in accordance with the NYSE rules because WCH currently owns approximately 8.05% of our outstanding
common stock (based on 608,725,020 shares outstanding as of January 15, 2009) and thus is a &#147;substantial security holder&#148; as defined in the NYSE rules. </FONT></P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_4"></A>Effects on Our Stockholders of Our Issuance of the Shares, the Warrants and the Warrant Shares to WCH </B></FONT></P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Pursuant to the Master Transaction Agreement, WCH will purchase (i)&nbsp;58,000,000 shares of our common stock and (ii)&nbsp;Warrants to purchase 35,000,000 shares of our common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per
share (as adjusted pursuant to the terms of the Warrants) for an aggregate purchase price equal to (a) 58,000,000 multiplied by (b) the lesser of (A) the average of the closing prices per share of our common stock on the New York Stock Exchange (the
&#147;<B><I>NYSE</I></B>&#148;) for the twenty (20) trading days immediately prior to and including December 12, 2008 and (B) the average of the closing prices per share of our common stock on the NYSE for the twenty (20) trading days immediately
prior to the closing date of the Transactions. We will issue the Warrant Shares upon exercise by WCH of the Warrants. Upon issuance of the Shares at the Closing, WCH will own approximately 16.05% of the outstanding shares of our common stock, based
on 608,725,020 shares outstanding as of January 15, 2009. If WCH exercises the Warrants in full when the Warrants become exercisable, WCH will own approximately 19.9% of our common stock on a fully diluted basis (including outstanding stock options
and restricted stock units, based on 608,725,020 shares outstanding as of January 15, 2009). Stockholders should consider the following factors which may affect them, as well as the other information contained in this proxy statement, in evaluating
the proposal to approve the issuance of the Shares and the Warrants pursuant to the Master Transaction Agreement and the issuance of the Warrant Shares upon exercise of the Warrants. </FONT></P>  <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Possible effect on market price of our common stock.</I>&nbsp;We are unable to predict the potential effects of the Transactions on the trading
activity and market price of our common stock. We are also unable to predict the effects on the trading activity and market price of our common stock if the Transactions do not close. Sales by WCH of a substantial number of shares of our common
stock in the public market, or the perception that such sales might occur, could cause the price of our common stock to decline. Other than securities law requirements, there are only limited restrictions on WCH&#146;s sales of the Shares, Warrants
and Warrant Shares. See &#147;The Master Transaction Agreement&#151;Transfer Restrictions&#148; included elsewhere in this proxy statement. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><I>WCH will increase its ownership in our common stock and will have a right to designate one person for election to our board of directors.</I>&nbsp;Following the Closing and when the Warrants become exercisable, assuming exercise of the
Warrants, WCH will beneficially own approximately 19.9% of our common stock on a fully diluted basis (including outstanding stock options and restricted stock units) and would be our largest stockholder. As a result of the Transactions, WCH will
increase its ability to influence matters submitted to our stockholders for a vote. Pursuant to the Master Transaction Agreement, for so long as WCH and its permitted transferees beneficially own at least 10% of our outstanding common stock, WCH has
the right to designate one person for election to our board of directors. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">6 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Dilution.</I>&nbsp;The issuance of the Shares and Warrant Shares to WCH will have a dilutive effect on
an individual stockholder&#146;s percentage voting power. Our issuance of the Shares to WCH will also have a dilutive effect on our future net income per common share. Our issuance of the Warrants to WCH will have a dilutive effect on our future net
income per common share when the Warrants become exercisable, and after the Warrants are exercised, the Warrant Shares issuable upon exercise of the Warrants will have a dilutive effect on our future net income per common share. In addition, the
standstill provisions in the Master Transaction Agreement permit WCH to acquire additional shares of our common stock up to a limit of 22.5% in the aggregate of our voting securities during the five years after the Closing, and this ownership
percentage limitation terminates after this five-year period. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_5"></A>The Parties </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>AMD</I>. We are a global semiconductor company with facilities around the world. Our products consist of (i)&nbsp;x86 microprocessors, for the
commercial and consumer markets, embedded microprocessors for commercial, commercial client and consumer markets and chipsets for desktop and notebook personal computers, professional workstations and servers and (ii)&nbsp;graphics, video and
multimedia products for desktop and notebook computers, including home media PCs, professional workstations and servers and technology for game consoles. </FONT></P>  <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Mubadala and WCH.</I>&nbsp;WCH is an exempted limited partnership organized under the laws of the Cayman Islands. Mubadala owns all of the partnership interests in WCH. AMD and WCH are parties to a stock purchase
agreement dated as of November&nbsp;15, 2007, pursuant to which AMD issued and sold to WCH 49,000,000 shares of our common stock for an aggregate purchase price of $622.3 million, less an expense reimbursement of approximately $14.6 million (the
&#147;<B><I>2007 Investment</I></B>&#148;). As a result of the 2007 Investment, WCH owns approximately 8.05% of the outstanding shares of our common stock, based on 608,725,020 shares outstanding as of January 15, 2009. </FONT></P>  <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Mubadala is an investment and development company wholly owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi. Mubadala&#146;s mandate is to generate sustainable
economic benefits for Abu Dhabi through prudent, commercially viable and profitable business ventures. Mubadala was established as an Abu Dhabi public joint stock company. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>ATIC.</I>&nbsp;ATIC is a limited liability company established under the laws of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and wholly owned by the Government of Abu
Dhabi. ATIC is focused on making significant investments in the advanced technology sector, both locally and internationally. Its mandate is to generate returns that deliver long-term benefits to the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. We have been informed by
ATIC that it is anticipated that, prior to the Closing, ATIC will become an Abu Dhabi public joint stock company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>The Foundry
Company</I>. The Foundry Company, an exempted company incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands (&#147;<B><I>The Foundry Company</I></B>&#148;), will be a U.S.-headquartered, leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing joint venture between
ATIC and AMD. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_6"></A>The Transactions </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Pursuant to the Master Transaction Agreement, AMD and ATIC will form a manufacturing joint venture, The Foundry Company. AMD will contribute certain assets and liabilities to The Foundry Company in exchange for
certain securities of The Foundry Company, ATIC will contribute cash to The Foundry Company and pay cash to AMD in exchange for certain securities of The Foundry Company, and WCH will purchase the Shares and the Warrants from AMD. As of September
27, 2008, the book value of the assets to be contributed by AMD to The Foundry Company was approximately $4.0&nbsp;billion out of AMD&#146;s approximately $9.4&nbsp;billion of assets. AMD will also transfer all non-patent intellectual property
related exclusively to manufacturing and will transfer patents related to its manufacturing and microprocessor business that are approximately equal in value to those being retained. However, no patents related to AMD&#146;s graphics business will
be transferred. The Foundry Company will manufacture semiconductor products and will provide certain foundry services to AMD and in the future will offer foundry services to other third-party customers. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">7 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Master Transaction Agreement contemplates that AMD, ATIC and The Foundry Company will enter into a
Shareholders&#146; Agreement (the &#147;<B><I>Shareholders&#146; Agreement</I></B>&#148;), which sets forth the rights and obligations of AMD and ATIC as shareholders of The Foundry Company. In addition, a Funding Agreement among AMD, ATIC and The
Foundry Company (the &#147;<B><I>Funding Agreement</I></B>&#148;) will provide for further equity funding of The Foundry Company by ATIC of a minimum of $3.6 billion and up to $6.0 billion over the five years after the Closing, and a Wafer Supply
Agreement between AMD and The Foundry Company (the &#147;<B><I>Wafer Supply</I></B> <B><I>Agreement</I></B>&#148;) will govern the terms by which AMD will purchase products manufactured by The Foundry Company. The Foundry Company will manufacture
semiconductor products using intellectual property transferred by AMD to The Foundry Company, and certain intellectual property licensed by AMD. For more information on these agreements, see &#147;The Shareholders&#146; Agreement,&#148; &#147;The
Funding Agreement,&#148; &#147;The Wafer Supply Agreement&#148; and &#147;Agreements Related to Intellectual Property&#148; appearing elsewhere in this proxy statement. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_7"></A>Our Purpose and Reasons for the Transactions </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The semiconductor industry is
undergoing a profound transformation. Vertically integrated companies are abandoning plans to invest in new capacity and manufacturing technology while announcing plans to outsource a growing percentage of their wafer requirements. Captive volumes
can no longer support the cost of building leading-edge capacity and process technology investments. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our board of directors held various
discussions and consulted with our management and financial, legal and other advisors and believes that the Transactions will benefit AMD stockholders in a number of ways: </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

accounts of The Foundry Company after the Closing, because we will be transferring the subsidiary that owes $1.2 billion of indebtedness to The Foundry Company at Closing, we will no longer be obligated to repay that $1.2 billion of indebtedness

a fabless business model. We believe the number of IDMs foregoing their own manufacturing capabilities will continue to increase, which would result in higher demand for foundry services. The Foundry Company should, and is designed to, be in a

profits will be eliminated and ATIC&#146;s noncontrolling interest, represented by its equity interests in The Foundry Company, will not be recorded on our consolidated balance sheet as stockholders&#146; equity due to the right that ATIC has to put
those securities back to us in the event of a change of control of AMD. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Our net income per common share will consist of our consolidated

complex considerations and judgments concerning differences in financial and operating characteristics of the companies involved in these transactions and other factors that could affect the transaction multiples in such transactions to which the
Master Transaction Agreement is being compared. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Discounted Cash Flow Analysis </I></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Merrill Lynch performed a discounted cash flow analysis of The Foundry Company for the period January&nbsp;1, 2009 through December&nbsp;31, 2020 based on
management projections. Merrill Lynch calculated ranges of enterprise value based upon the sum of the discounted net present value of The Foundry Company&#146;s eleven year stream of projected unlevered free cash flows plus the discounted net
present value of the terminal value based on a range of multiples applied to The Foundry Company&#146;s projected 2020 EBITDA. In its discounted cash flow analysis, Merrill Lynch performed sensitivities based upon the attainment of varying amounts
of third-party customer revenue and applied what it considered to be appropriate discount rates ranging from 20.0% to 30.0% and terminal value multiples of estimated calendar year 2020 EBITDA ranging from 2.0x to 5.0x, both of which ranges were
based on attainment of third-party customer revenue. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Using the discount rates and terminal value multiples of estimated calendar year 2020

a complex process involving various determinations as to the most appropriate and relevant methods of financial analysis and the application of those methods to the particular circumstances; therefore, such an opinion is not readily susceptible to
partial analysis or summary description. No company, business or transaction used in such analyses as a comparison is identical to the Business, The Foundry Company or the Master Transaction Agreement, nor is an evaluation of such analyses entirely
mathematical. In arriving at its opinion, Merrill Lynch did not attribute any particular weight to any analysis or factor considered by it, but rather made qualitative judgments as to the significance and relevance of each analysis and factor.

Company Consideration</I></B>&#148;). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">No company utilized in the comparable company analysis is identical to The Foundry Company. In
evaluating comparable companies, Morgan Stanley made judgments and assumptions with regard to industry performance, general business, economic, market and financial conditions and other matters, many of which are beyond the control of The Foundry
Company and AMD, such as the impact of competition on the businesses of AMD and The Foundry Company and the industry generally, industry growth and the absence of any adverse material change in the financial condition and prospects of AMD, The
Foundry Company or the industry or in the financial markets in general. Mathematical analysis (such as determining the average or median) is not in itself a meaningful method of using peer group data. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Discounted Cash Flow Analysis </I></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As
part of its analysis, and in order to estimate a range of aggregate present values for The Foundry Company, Morgan Stanley performed a discounted cash flow analysis. A discounted cash flow analysis is designed to provide insight into the value of a
company as a function of its future cash flows and terminal value. Morgan Stanley relied on cash flow projections for calendar years 2009 through 2013 for The Foundry Company provided by the management of AMD. Morgan Stanley estimated a range of
terminal values calculated in 2013 based on EBITDA exit multiples of 3.5x to 4.5x applied to 2014 EBITDA. &#147;Terminal value&#148; refers to the estimate of the value of all future cash flows from an asset at a particular point in time. Morgan
Stanley discounted the unlevered free cash flow streams and the estimated range of terminal values to a present value, as of December&nbsp;31, 2008, based on (i)&nbsp;a discount rate range of 15% to 25% for the portion of The Foundry Company&#146;s
unlevered free cash flow associated with manufacturing AMD microprocessors, (ii)&nbsp;a discount rate range of 25% to 30% for the unlevered free cash flow associated with The Foundry Company&#146;s business focused on third-party semiconductor
customers other than AMD, and (iii)&nbsp;a discount rate of 25% for the terminal value. Based on these projections and assumptions, the discounted cash flow analysis of The Foundry Company yielded an implied aggregate valuation range of
approximately $1.2 billion to $3.4 billion. Morgan Stanley noted that the value of net tangible assets contributed by AMD was $2.1 billion and the value of the Foundry Company Consideration to be received by AMD pursuant to the Master Transaction
Agreement was $3.1 billion. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Analysis of Precedent Transactions </I></FONT></P> <P

Foundry Company Employment Agreement will be automatically null and void. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Under the Ruiz Foundry Company Employment Agreement

opportunity at 400% of his base salary, subject to achievement of applicable performance goals established by The Foundry Company Board in consultation with Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz. In the event that Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz&#146;s employment is terminated by The
Foundry Company without Cause (as such term is defined in the Ruiz Foundry Company Employment Agreement) or Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz resigns for Good Reason (as such term is defined in the Ruiz Foundry Company Employment Agreement), The Foundry Company will
pay to Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz, subject to compliance with a non-competition and non-solicitation provisions and execution of a release of claims, an amount equal to his base salary and the target annual bonuses remaining payable to Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz for the
remainder of the Ruiz Employment Term, payable in a lump sum. If Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz&#146;s employment is terminated due to disability or death, Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz or his beneficiaries, as applicable, are eligible to receive the same amounts as if
Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz had been terminated without Cause; provided that no release of claims is required in the event that Dr.&nbsp;Ruiz&#146;s employment is terminated due to death. </FONT></P> <P

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_24"></A>WCH Standstill Respecting AMD </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">For a period of five years (or sooner, if WCH and its transferees cease to own at least 10% of AMD&#146;s voting securities), WCH, ATIC and their
transferees and affiliates will not, without AMD&#146;s consent, seek to acquire more than 22.5% of the voting securities of AMD, or initiate, or induce or attempt to induce any third person to initiate, any extraordinary corporate transaction
involving AMD (including a merger, sale of assets, restructuring or liquidation), or to seek to or participate in any attempt to cause a change of control of the management or board of directors of AMD, or take any other similar actions, including a
public announcement of any such plans, or advise, assist or encourage any other persons in connection with any of the foregoing. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">ATIC and
WCH also agree during such period not to request that AMD waive any of the foregoing provisions, although ATIC or WCH may ask AMD whether AMD would wish to entertain a proposal for the acquisition of AMD, but may not make such a proposal absent
AMD&#146;s affirmative response to such question. The standstill does not prevent ATIC or WCH from voting any securities at their sole discretion on matters submitted to the stockholders of AMD for a vote, or from voting in favor of, or tendering
any AMD securities held by any of them into, any extraordinary transaction involving AMD or a substantial portion of its securities or assets. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_25">
</A>WCH Transfer Restrictions on AMD Securities </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Until such time WCH and its permitted transferees beneficially own, in the aggregate,
less than 10% of the outstanding shares of our common stock, WCH and such permitted transferees may only resell shares of our common stock (i)&nbsp;in connection with a bona fide pledge or transfer in connection with a financing transaction secured
by a pledge of WCH&#146;s AMD common stock, (ii)&nbsp;by means of an underwritten public offering pursuant to an effective registration statement under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#147;<B><I>Securities Act</I></B>&#148;), or
(iii)&nbsp;pursuant to Rule 144 promulgated under the Securities Act. Notwithstanding the foregoing, WCH or its permitted transferees may sell or transfer AMD common stock to any other permitted transferee. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_26"></A>Employees </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Foundry
Company will extend, or will cause its applicable subsidiaries to extend, offers of employment to certain AMD employees (the &#147;<B><I>Transferred Employees</I></B>&#148;) at least 30 days prior to Closing and will hire, or cause its applicable

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_30"></A>THE SHAREHOLDERS&#146; AGREEMENT </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The rights and obligations of AMD and ATIC, as shareholders of The Foundry Company (each, a &#147;<B><I>Foundry Company Shareholder</I></B>&#148;), are
set forth in the Shareholders&#146; Agreement. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_31"></A>Board of Directors </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Foundry Company board of directors (the &#147;<B><I>The Foundry Company Board</I></B>&#148;) will consist of eight directors, and, because AMD and
ATIC each own 50% of the shares entitled to vote in the election of directors and pursuant to the Shareholders&#146; Agreement, AMD and ATIC will each be entitled to designate for nomination four directors. The 50/50 ownership of the voting shares
and rights of each of AMD and ATIC to designate four directors will not change until the occurrence of the Reconciliation Event. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">&#147;<B><I>Reconciliation Event</I></B>&#148; means the earlier of (i)&nbsp;such time when AMD has secured for The Foundry Company the right to make unlimited volumes of products, including microprocessors, for AMD and its subsidiaries,
regardless of whether The Foundry Company is a &#147;Subsidiary&#148; or &#147;Affiliate&#148; of AMD for purposes of the Intel Patent Cross License Agreement, or (ii)&nbsp;such time when The Foundry Company Board determines that The Foundry Company
no longer needs to be a &#147;Subsidiary&#148; of AMD as defined in Section&nbsp;1.22 of the Intel Patent Cross License Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, notwithstanding any provision of the Shareholders&#146; Agreement or any other document
related to the Transactions, prior to the Reconciliation Event, The Foundry Company will in no event be under any obligation (contractually or otherwise) to directly or indirectly distribute more than 70% of its profits to any person or entity.
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Only after a Reconciliation Event, the number of directors a Foundry Company Shareholder may designate will be adjusted as follows:
(i)&nbsp;a Foundry Company Shareholder holding 30% or more but less than 40% of the fully diluted shares will be entitled to designate three directors; (ii)&nbsp;a Foundry Company Shareholder holding 20% or more but less than 30% of the fully
diluted shares will be entitled to designate two directors; (iii)&nbsp;a Foundry Company Shareholder holding 10% or more but less than 20% of the fully diluted shares will be entitled to designate one director; and (iv)&nbsp;a Foundry Company
Shareholder holding less than 10% of the fully diluted shares will have no right to designate any directors. To the extent the number of directors a Foundry Company Shareholder is entitled to nominate is reduced as a result of a decrease in such
Foundry Company Shareholder&#146;s ownership of The Foundry Company, then, so long as the other Foundry Company Shareholder owns at least a majority of the fully diluted shares of The Foundry Company, such other Foundry Company Shareholder will be
entitled to designate all of the remaining directors. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_32"></A>Officers </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The initial Chief Executive Officer of The Foundry Company will be Douglas Grose, and ATIC will designate the initial Chief Financial Officer. The other
officers of The Foundry Company will be appointed by a committee of The Foundry Company Board. Hector de J. Ruiz will be Chairman of The Foundry Company Board, which is a non-director and non-voting position. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_33"></A>Voting </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The share capital
of The Foundry Company at the Closing will consist of (i)&nbsp;Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares (the &#147;<B><I>Class A Ordinary Shares</I></B>&#148;), of which two shares will be outstanding (one issued to each of AMD and ATIC); (ii)&nbsp;Class B
Ordinary Shares (the &#147;<B><I>Class B Ordinary Shares</I></B>&#148;); (iii)&nbsp;Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares (the &#147;<B><I>Class A Preferred Shares</I></B>&#148;) and (iv)&nbsp;Class B Preferred Shares (the &#147;<B><I>Class B Preferred
Shares</I></B>&#148;). Prior to the Reconciliation Event, the Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares, the Class B Preferred Shares and the Class B Ordinary Shares will be non-voting and only the Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares will have voting rights of one
vote per Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Share. Following the Reconciliation Event, the Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares will be automatically redeemed and the voting rights of the Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares, the Class B Preferred Shares and the Class B
Ordinary Shares will be given effect. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_35"></A>Transfer Restrictions </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><I>Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares.</I> Each of AMD and ATIC will own one Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Share. Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares are the only voting securities of The Foundry Company prior to the Reconciliation Event. The Foundry Company
Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares are non-transferable. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Other Foundry Company Securities.</I> With respect to the other securities of The
Foundry Company (Class A Preferred Shares, Class B Preferred Shares, the Class B Ordinary Shares and the Convertible Notes), no Foundry Company Shareholder may sell any of such Foundry Company securities, without the consent of the other Foundry
Company Shareholder, if (i)&nbsp;prior to the Reconciliation Event, the sale of such securities would cause The Foundry Company to fail to constitute a &#147;Subsidiary&#148; of AMD under the Intel Patent Cross License Agreement, (ii)&nbsp;such sale
is made to Intel or any of its affiliates or (iii)&nbsp;such sale is made to a competitor of The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, each
Foundry Company Shareholder agrees not to sell, transfer or encumber any such Foundry Company securities prior to the Restricted Period. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">The following transfers of such securities of The Foundry Company are exempt from the above transfer restrictions: (a)&nbsp;transfers with the prior written consent of the other Foundry Company Shareholder; (b)&nbsp;a transfer to a
permitted transferee or to the other Foundry Company Shareholder; (c)&nbsp;the sale of up to 25% of a Foundry Company Shareholder&#146;s fully diluted shares in an initial public offering of The Foundry Company (<B><I>&#147;IPO&#148;</I></B>); and
(d)&nbsp;in each year following the IPO, the sale of up to 25% of a Foundry Company Shareholder&#146;s fully diluted shares through a public offering or Rule 144 under the Securities Act. However, AMD&#146;s rights to sell such securities of The
Foundry Company as set forth in (c)&nbsp;and (d)&nbsp;above will be suspended until the Reconciliation Event has occurred. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">
<FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Shareholder of the offer, and the non-selling Foundry Company Shareholder will have 30 days to purchase the offered securities. In addition, a Foundry
Company Shareholder cannot consummate a sale of securities of The Foundry Company to a third party without offering such securities for sale to the other Foundry Company Shareholder at least 10 business days prior to the contemplated consummation of
the sale of such securities to the third party. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_37"></A>Tag-Along Rights </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Following the end of the Restricted Period, no Foundry Company Shareholder may sell more than 10% of its fully diluted securities of The Foundry Company
unless the other Foundry Company Shareholder is offered the right and option to sell the same percentage of securities held by it. This right terminates upon an IPO. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_38"></A>Drag-Along Rights </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Following the end of the Restricted Period, if a Foundry
Company Shareholder holding at least 75% of the fully diluted shares of The Foundry Company proposes to sell all of its securities of The Foundry Company to a third party, such Foundry Company Shareholder will have the right to require the other
Foundry Company Shareholder to sell all of its securities of The Foundry Company to the third party for the same consideration and on the same terms. This right terminates upon an IPO. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_39"></A>AMD Change of Control </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In the event of a change of control of AMD without
ATIC&#146;s prior written consent: (i)&nbsp;all transfer restrictions with respect to securities of The Foundry Company held by ATIC and its permitted transferees will terminate; (ii)&nbsp;if such change of control occurs prior to the IPO, ATIC will
have the right to require The Foundry Company to consummate the IPO and to register ATIC&#146;s securities of The Foundry Company in connection with such IPO; (iii)&nbsp;(A)&nbsp;ATIC will have a put right to sell all of its securities of The
Foundry Company to AMD if the change of control occurs within 24 months of the Closing or (B)&nbsp;if the change of control occurs after the Reconciliation Event, ATIC will have the option to purchase all of the securities of The Foundry Company
held by AMD and its permitted transferees, in each case at fair market value; (iv)&nbsp;until the end of 2013, as long as ATIC owns any securities of The Foundry Company, ATIC has the right to require AMD or any counterparty to an AMD change of
control transaction to assume a portion of ATIC&#146;s funding commitment under the Funding Agreement based on the percentage of fully diluted shares held by AMD on each &#147;Funding Date&#148; (as such term is defined in the Funding Agreement);
and (v)&nbsp;as long as ATIC owns any securities of The Foundry Company, ATIC has the right to require any counterparty to an AMD change of control transaction to guarantee all of AMD&#146;s obligations under the documents related to the
Transactions. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_40"></A>Rights to Purchase New Shares </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Foundry Company must offer each Foundry Company Shareholder the right to purchase its pro rata share of any securities of The Foundry Company in the event The Foundry Company proposes to issue new shares to a
third party. This right terminates upon an IPO. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_41"></A>Termination </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Shareholders&#146; Agreement may be terminated (i)&nbsp;upon dissolution of The Foundry Company, (ii)&nbsp;by the written agreement of all parties to
the Shareholders&#146; Agreement, (iii)&nbsp;at the election of a Foundry Company Shareholder upon certain events of bankruptcy of the other Foundry Company Shareholder or (iv)&nbsp;with respect to any Foundry Company Shareholder, at such time a
Foundry Company Shareholder ceases to own any securities of The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The foregoing description of the Shareholders&#146;

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_42"></A>THE FUNDING AGREEMENT </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Funding Agreement provides for the further funding of The Foundry Company. Pursuant to the Funding Agreement, ATIC has committed to additional equity
funding of a minimum of $3.6 billion and up to $6.0 billion over the five years after the Closing. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_43"></A>Annual Business Plan </B>
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Foundry Company management team must present its annual business plan (the &#147;<B><I>Annual Business Plan</I></B>&#148;) to The
Foundry Company Board for approval on or prior to mid-November of each fiscal year, which date will be prior to the end of the seventh fiscal week of the fourth fiscal quarter of The Foundry Company. The Annual Business Plan must include estimates
of the sources and uses of funds necessary to conduct The Foundry Company&#146;s business by fiscal quarter as well as estimated third-party debt financing. In the event The Foundry Company Board does not approve the Annual Business Plan within a
certain time frame, the Funding Agreement sets forth procedures by which a resolution to any deadlock may be obtained, and the conditions under which ATIC may continue its funding commitments despite the deadlock. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_44"></A>Cash Reserve </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Foundry
Company must maintain a cash reserve amount equal to at least $1 billion at all times during the term of the Funding Agreement, provided, however, that this requirement shall no longer apply upon the earlier of (i)&nbsp;The Foundry Company entering
into a Transition Period (as defined below) or (ii)&nbsp;the end of Phase II (as defined below). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_45"></A>Funding </B></FONT></P> <P

Preferred Shares. See &#147;Description of The Foundry Company Share Capital&#148; elsewhere in this proxy statement. Under certain circumstances, The Foundry Company will issue convertible notes to ATIC in lieu of Class&nbsp;A and Class B Preferred
Shares. See &#147;Description of Foundry Company Convertible Subordinated Notes&#148; elsewhere in this proxy statement. The aggregate amount of equity funding to be provided by the Foundry Company Shareholders in any fiscal year depends on the time
period of such funding (Phase I, II or III) and the amounts set forth in the five-year capital plan of The Foundry Company. The Phases are defined as follows: </FONT></P> <P STYLE="font-size:6px;margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px">&nbsp;</P>

Agreement (the &#147;<B><I>Phase I Funding Conditions</I></B>&#148;). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">With respect to Phase II, in addition to the conditions for Phase I,

Foundry Company will have achieved certain strategic milestones relating to the groundbreaking and build out of the Abu Dhabi fab and to AMD technology and the timing of the receipt by The Foundry Company of third party customer interest and revenue
(the &#147;<B><I>Phase II Funding Conditions</I></B>&#148;). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">With respect to Phase III, in addition to the conditions for Phase I,

able to approve the Annual Business Plan for the fiscal year ending in 2010, ATIC will be obligated to, and AMD may if it elects to, continue to fund at the original funding level set forth in the five-year capital plan (the &#147;<B><I>Original
Funding Level</I></B>&#148;), through the end of Phase I, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the General Funding Conditions and the Phase I Funding Conditions. If at the end of such fiscal year, the Annual Business Plan for the fiscal year
ending in 2011 is approved in accordance with the Funding Agreement and the Shareholders&#146; Agreement, then funding will be at the Original Funding Level, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the General Funding Conditions and the Phase I
Funding Conditions. If at the end of such fiscal year, the Annual Business Plan for the Fiscal Year ending in 2011 is not so approved, then the provisions for Phase II Business Plan Deadlock will apply. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Phase II Business Plan Deadlock</I>. In the event of a Business Plan Deadlock with respect to any fiscal year of Phase&nbsp;II, ATIC will continue to
provide funding in an amount at least equal to an amount which is intended to be sufficient to both (i)&nbsp;continue to meet AMD&#146;s volume requirements as set forth in the Wafer Supply Agreement and (ii)&nbsp;continue to build out both Fab 38
in Dresden and Fab 4x in New York to the capacities required to ensure continued availability of 100% of the Dresden and New York subsidies (such amount not to exceed $3.582 billion) (the &#147;<B><I>Minimum Funding Level</I></B>&#148;) and up to
the Original Funding Level, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the General Funding Conditions and the Phase II Funding Conditions, until either </FONT>

Transition Funding Level in the case of a Transition Period during Phase III, in each case subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the General Funding Conditions and the Phase I Funding Conditions on or prior to any funding date; (iv)&nbsp;the
Foundry Company Shareholders will jointly pursue, in good faith, transition options during the Transition Period, including without limitation, winding-down, selling or liquidating The Foundry Company; and (v)&nbsp;upon termination of the Transition
Period, ATIC will have the option to purchase in cash any or all securities of The Foundry Company held by AMD and its permitted transferees at a price equal to their fair market value. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_49"></A>THE WAFER SUPPLY AGREEMENT </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">AMD will purchase products manufactured by The Foundry Company pursuant to the terms of the Wafer Supply Agreement. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_50"></A>AMD Purchase Commitments </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><I>MPU Products</I>.<B> </B>AMD will purchase all of its and its subsidiaries&#146; microprocessor unit (&#147;<B><I>MPU</I></B>&#148;) products from The Foundry Company sales subsidiaries, subject to limited exceptions. Notwithstanding the
foregoing, if AMD acquires a third-party business that manufactures MPU products, AMD will have up to two years to transition the manufacture of such MPU products to The Foundry Company. Additionally, AMD and its subsidiaries may use another foundry
company as a second source for certain of its quarterly MPU product wafer requirements, and may source additional amounts from such foundry company to the extent The Foundry Company is unable to deliver products to AMD sufficient to meet AMD&#146;s
material customer commitments. AMD&#146;s ability to source MPU requirements with such foundry company terminates: (i)&nbsp;upon the occurrence of a specified event; or (ii)&nbsp;subject to a wind-down period, if such foundry company undergoes a
change of control resulting in another entity controlling a majority of such company&#146;s assets or equity interests related to the manufacture of products on behalf of AMD. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>GPU Products</I>.<B> </B>Once The Foundry Company establishes a 32 nm qualified process, AMD will purchase from The Foundry Company sales entities,
where competitive, specified percentages of its and its subsidiaries&#146; graphics processor unit (&#147;<B><I>GPU</I></B>&#148;) requirements, which percentage will increase linearly over a five-year period. AMD agrees not to sell, transfer or
dispose of all or substantially all of its or its subsidiaries&#146; assets related to GPU products and related technology to any third party without The Foundry Company&#146;s consent, unless the transferee agrees to be bound by the terms of the
Wafer Supply Agreement, including its minimum purchase obligations, where competitive, with respect to GPU products. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_51"></A>The
Foundry Company Capacity Commitment </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">After reviewing forecasts provided by AMD, as agreed by the parties, The Foundry Company will
allocate such additional capacity sufficient to produce the MPU product volumes set forth in rolling, binding forecasts. The parties will establish capacity requirements in advance for GPU products. The Foundry Company will use commercially
reasonable efforts to fill any capacity allocated to but unutilized by AMD with production for third parties so as to offset and reduce AMD&#146;s fixed cost reimbursement obligations to The Foundry Company; provided that such efforts will not be
required if there exists any unutilized capacity that has not been allocated to AMD. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_52"></A>Management </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">A partnership committee comprised of an equal number of members appointed by each party will manage the relationship. Unresolved disputes will be
escalated to executive officers of each party for resolution. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_53"></A>Sort Services </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At AMD&#146;s request, The Foundry Company will provide sort services to AMD on a product by product basis. Sort equipment for MPU products will be
assigned to The Foundry Company on the effective date; in the event any sort equipment is no longer usable to provide sort services to AMD or The Foundry Company&#146;s other customers, The Foundry Company will dispose of such equipment and the
parties will determine the amount reimbursable to The Foundry Company or AMD. Additional AMD equipment may be consigned, and AMD will bear all the maintenance and operational costs for such equipment. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_54"></A>Pricing </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The price for MPU products is related to a certain percentage of The Foundry Company&#146;s MPU-specific total cost of goods sold. The price for GPU products will be determined on a product-by-product basis by the
parties. AMD will also be responsible for certain other cost reimbursements to The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_55"></A>Indemnification
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Foundry Company provides AMD and its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, successors and assigns with an
intellectual property infringement indemnity covering The Foundry Company&#146;s method of manufacturing the products, except for the methods specifically transferred to The Foundry Company on the effective date. AMD provides The Foundry Company and
its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, successors and assigns with an intellectual property infringement indemnity covering The Foundry Company&#146;s manufacture of wafers for AMD in compliance with any AMD product designs or
specifications, use of AMD&#146;s equipment, materials, methods and technologies as used by AMD immediately prior to the effective date, and use of property furnished by AMD in accordance with applicable standards and instructions. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_56"></A>Intellectual Property </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">AMD
grants The Foundry Company and applicable The Foundry Company subsidiaries and any permitted assignees a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free right and license to: (i)&nbsp;make products and import and sell such products to AMD; and
(ii)&nbsp;reproduce any documentation provided by AMD to enable The Foundry Company to manufacture such products for AMD. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_57"></A>Term; Termination </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Wafer Supply Agreement will be in effect no longer than 15 years after the
Closing. The Wafer Supply Agreement may be terminated at any time upon mutual written consent and may expire earlier upon the occurrence of certain events. The Wafer Supply Agreement may also be terminated if and when a business plan deadlock exists
and ATIC elects to enter into a transition period pursuant to the Funding Agreement. The Foundry Company will use commercially reasonable efforts to assist AMD to transition the supply of products to another provider, and continue to fulfill
purchase orders for up to two years following the termination or expiration of the Wafer Supply Agreement. During such transition period, pricing for MPU products will remain as set forth in the Wafer Supply Agreement, but AMD&#146;s purchase
commitments to The Foundry Company will no longer apply. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The foregoing description of the Wafer Supply Agreement is qualified in its
entirety by reference to the full text of the Wafer Supply Agreement, attached hereto as <B><I>Exhibit D</I></B>. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_58"></A>AGREEMENTS RELATED TO INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In connection with the Transactions, AMD and The Foundry Company will also enter into intellectual property related arrangements. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_59"></A>Patent Cross License Agreement </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">Pursuant to a Patent Cross License Agreement (the &#147;<B><I>Patent Cross License Agreement</I></B>&#148;), AMD and The Foundry Company will each grant to the other a non-exclusive license under patents which were filed by a party (or are
otherwise acquired by a party) within a certain number of years following the effective date of the Patent Cross License Agreement. AMD and The Foundry Company are also entering into arrangements under which all issued patents and pending patent
applications of AMD and its subsidiaries (other than patents and applications owned by ATI Technologies LLC and its wholly owned subsidiaries) will be divided between AMD and The Foundry Company. The Foundry Company will take ownership of its
allocation of patents and applications subject to pre-existing rights, licenses or immunities granted to third parties relating to such patents and applications. The patents and patent applications owned by each party after the division will be
licensed to the other party pursuant to the Patent Cross License Agreement. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_60"></A>Non-Patent Intellectual Property and Technology
Transfer Agreement </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Pursuant to a Non-Patent Intellectual Property and Technology Transfer Agreement, AMD will assign to The Foundry
Company all of its right, title and interest in technology and non-patent intellectual property rights used exclusively in the manufacture, sorting and/or intermediate (WIP) testing of semiconductor products. Technology and non-patent intellectual
property rights used exclusively in the design and/or post-delivery testing of semiconductor products will be retained by AMD. Technology and non-patent intellectual property rights used both in the manufacture, sorting and/or intermediate (WIP)
testing of semiconductor products and in the design and/or post-delivery testing of semiconductor products will be jointly owned by AMD and The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_61"></A>DESCRIPTION OF THE FOUNDRY COMPANY CONVERTIBLE SUBORDINATED NOTES
</B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">At Closing, in consideration for ATIC&#146;s cash contribution to The Foundry Company, The Foundry Company will issue convertible
subordinated notes convertible into Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares (the &#147;<B><I>Class A Convertible Notes</I></B>&#148;) and Class B Preferred Shares (the &#147;<B><I>Class B Convertible Notes</I></B>&#148;) to ATIC. In addition, prior to the
Reconciliation Event, to the extent that the issuance of any securities to ATIC in connection with an equity funding of The Foundry Company would cause The Foundry Company to fail to constitute a &#147;Subsidiary&#148; of AMD, as such term is
defined in the Intel Patent Cross License Agreement, The Foundry Company will instead issue to ATIC (i)&nbsp;additional Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes in an aggregate principal amount equal to the aggregate purchase price for the Class&nbsp;A
Preferred Shares that would have been issued to ATIC but for such provision, and (ii)&nbsp;additional Class B Convertible Notes in an aggregate principal amount equal to the aggregate purchase price for the Class B Preferred Shares that would have
been issued to ATIC but for such provision. The principal terms of the Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes and the Class B Convertible Notes are set forth below. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_62"></A>Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Interest</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes accrue
interest at a rate of 4%&nbsp;per annum, compounded semiannually, and payable semiannually in additional Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2"><I>Maturity</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes mature upon the later of (i)&nbsp;10 years from the date of issuance or (ii)&nbsp;the date of the Reconciliation Event. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Security</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes are the unsecured obligations of The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Ranking</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes will constitute a subordinated obligation of The Foundry Company and will rank subordinated in right
of payment to any current or future senior indebtedness of The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Redemption</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes are
not redeemable by The Foundry Company without the noteholder&#146;s consent. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Conversion</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes are
convertible, in whole or in part, in multiples of $1,000, into The Foundry Company Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares at the option of the holder at any time prior to the close of business on the business day immediately preceding the maturity date , at
the Conversion Ratio (as defined below) in effect on the date of conversion, if (i)&nbsp;such conversion would not cause The Foundry Company to fail to constitute a &#147;Subsidiary&#148; of AMD under the Intel Patent Cross License Agreement or
(ii)&nbsp;the Reconciliation Event has occurred. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">On or after the Reconciliation Event, the Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes will
automatically convert into Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares of The Foundry Company upon the earlier of (i)&nbsp;a Foundry Company IPO, (ii)&nbsp;certain change of control transactions of The Foundry Company or (iii)&nbsp;the close of business on the
business day immediately preceding the maturity date. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The &#147;<B><I>Conversion Ratio</I></B>&#148; for each $1,000 principal amount of
Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes will be a number obtained by dividing (1)&nbsp;$1,000 by (2)&nbsp;the applicable Class&nbsp;A Convertible Notes Conversion Price (as hereinafter defined) in effect at the time of conversion. The &#147;<B><I>Class A
Convertible Notes Conversion Price</I></B>&#148; will initially be the per share price of the Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares at the time the Class&nbsp;A Convertible Note was issued, subject to customary anti-dilution adjustments. The Foundry Company
will deliver cash in lieu of any fractional shares upon conversion. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Events of Default</I>. The following constitute an event of default

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_64"></A>DESCRIPTION OF THE FOUNDRY COMPANY SHARE CAPITAL </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_65"></A>Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">The Foundry Company will issue two Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares, one to each of AMD and ATIC. The Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares will carry one vote each and will be the only voting securities of The Foundry Company prior to the
Reconciliation Event. Following the Reconciliation Event, the Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares will be redeemed by The Foundry Company. The Class&nbsp;A Ordinary Shares are non-transferable. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_66"></A>Class B Ordinary Shares </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Foundry Company will issue Class B Ordinary
Shares at the Closing. The Class B Ordinary Shares will be non-voting until the Reconciliation Event. Following the Reconciliation Event, each holder of Class B Ordinary Shares will be entitled to one vote per Class B Ordinary Share. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:18px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_67"></A>Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares </B></FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman"
SIZE="2">The Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares to be issued by The Foundry Company in connection with any equity funding under the Funding Agreement will have the following principal terms: </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Ranking</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares will rank senior in right of payment to the Ordinary Shares of The Foundry Company and junior in right
of payment to the Class&nbsp;B Preferred Shares of The Foundry Company for purposes of dividends, distributions and upon a Liquidation Event (as defined below). </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Accretion</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares will not be entitled to any dividend or pre-determined accretion in value. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT
FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Liquidation Preference</I>. In the event of the liquidation, dissolution or winding up of The Foundry Company (a <B><I>&#147;Liquidation Event&#148;</I></B>), each Class&nbsp;A Preferred Share will be entitled to
receive, after the distribution to the holders of the Class B Preferred Shares but prior to any distribution to the holders of Ordinary Shares, out of the remaining assets of The Foundry Company, if any, an amount equal to the initial purchase price
per share of the Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares. Upon completion of the above distributions to the holders of Preferred Shares, all of the remaining assets of The Foundry Company, if any, will be distributed pro rata among the holders of Ordinary
Shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Conversion</I>. Each Class&nbsp;A Preferred Share will be convertible, at the option of the holder thereof, into Class B
Ordinary Shares at the then applicable Class&nbsp;A Conversion Rate (as hereinafter defined) upon a Liquidation Event. Each Class&nbsp;A Preferred Share will automatically convert into Class B Ordinary Shares at the then applicable Class&nbsp;A
Conversion Rate upon the earlier of (i)&nbsp;a Foundry Company IPO or (ii)&nbsp;a change of control transaction of The Foundry Company. The &#147;<B><I>Class A Conversion Rate</I></B>&#148; will initially be 100 Class B Ordinary Shares for each
Class&nbsp;A Preferred Share converted, subject to customary anti-dilution adjustments. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Redemption</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Preferred
Shares will not be redeemable by The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Voting Rights</I>. The Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares will be non-voting until the
Reconciliation Event. Following the Reconciliation Event, each Class&nbsp;A Preferred Share will vote on an as-converted basis with the Ordinary Shares, voting together as a single class, with respect to any question upon which holders of Ordinary
Shares have the right to vote. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">45 </FONT></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B><A NAME="rom61725_68"></A>Class B Preferred Shares </B></FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Class B Preferred Shares to be issued by The Foundry Company in connection with any equity funding will have the following principal terms:
</FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Ranking</I>. The Class B Preferred Shares will rank senior in right of payment to all other classes or series of equity securities of
The Foundry Company for purposes of dividends, distributions and upon a Liquidation Event. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Accretion</I>. Each Class B Preferred Share
will be deemed to accrete in value at a rate of 12%&nbsp;per year, compounded semiannually, of the initial purchase price per such share (the sum of the initial purchase price per such share plus the amount of value accreted on such share is
hereinafter referred to as the &#147;<B><I>Accreted Value</I></B>&#148;). Such Accreted Value will accrue daily from and after the issue date of such share and will be taken into account upon certain distributions to the holders of Class B Preferred
Shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In the event that the aggregate Accreted Value in respect of all Class B Preferred Shares held by ATIC, when taken together with
any Class&nbsp;A Preferred Shares held by ATIC, would cause the aggregate economic interest of ATIC in The Foundry Company to exceed thresholds required for The Foundry Company to remain a &#147;Subsidiary&#148; of AMD under the Intel Patent Cross
License Agreement, such excess amount of the Accreted Value will be converted into Class B Convertible Notes that will only be payable in the event that Accreted Value is actually paid in the form of cash or Ordinary Shares and that any such payment
does not cause the economic interest thresholds required for the Foundry Company to remain a &#147;Subsidiary&#148; of AMD under the Intel Patent Cross License Agreement to be exceeded. </FONT></P> <P
STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Liquidation Preference</I>. In the event of a Liquidation Event, each Class B Preferred Share will be entitled to receive, prior to any distribution
to the holders of any other classes or series of equity securities, an amount equal to the Accreted Value of such share. Upon completion of the above distribution to the holders of Class B Preferred Shares, each Class&nbsp;A Preferred Share will be
entitled to receive its liquidation preference amount out of any remaining assets of The Foundry Company. Upon completion of the above distributions to the holders of Preferred Shares, all of the remaining assets of The Foundry Company, if any, will
be distributed pro rata among the holders of Ordinary Shares. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Conversion</I>. Each Class B Preferred Share will be convertible, at the
option of the holder thereof, into Class B Ordinary Shares at the then applicable Class B Conversion Rate (as hereinafter defined) upon a Liquidation Event. Each Class B Preferred Share will automatically convert into Class B Ordinary Shares at the
then applicable Class B Conversion Rate upon the earlier of (i)&nbsp;a Foundry Company IPO or (ii)&nbsp;a change of control transaction of The Foundry Company. The &#147;<B><I>Class B Conversion Rate</I></B>&#148; will initially be 100 Class B
Ordinary Shares for each Class B Preferred Share converted, subject to customary anti-dilution adjustments. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the resulting fair market value of the Class B Ordinary Shares to be received upon such conversion would be
less than the Accreted Value of such Class B Preferred Share, then the holder of such Class B Preferred Share will receive additional Class B Ordinary Shares upon such conversion in order to cause the fair market value of the total amount of Class B
Ordinary Shares to be received upon such conversion to equal the Accreted Value of such Class B Preferred Share. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Redemption</I>. The
Class B Preferred Shares will not be redeemable by The Foundry Company. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT FACE="Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><I>Voting Rights</I>. The Class B Preferred Shares will be
non-voting until the Reconciliation Event. Following the Reconciliation Event, each Class B Preferred Share will vote on an as-converted basis with the Ordinary Shares, voting together as a single class, with respect to any question upon which
holders of Ordinary Shares have the right to vote. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT SIZE="1">&nbsp;</FONT></P>

which may be outstanding. However, the terms of certain of our borrowing arrangements restrict our ability to declare or pay dividends on our common stock in certain circumstances. Upon liquidation or dissolution of the company subject to prior
liquidation rights of the holders of preferred stock, the holders of common stock are entitled to receive on a pro rata basis the remaining assets of the company available for distribution. Holders of common stock have no preemptive or other
subscription rights, and there are no conversion rights or redemption or sinking fund provisions with respect to such shares. All outstanding shares of common stock are fully paid and non-assessable. </FONT></P> <P
